summary: Two repairs in tools/audio/build.py with tests, then the processed downloads were rebuilt. (1) A one-shot whose envelope maximum lies inside the fade-out it would get now keeps the recording untouched and gets a 3 ms raised-cosine tail appended; only k_door_close_1 of the 29 one-shots is affected. Its gain is now -14.09 dB, the same the unprocessed recording needs (was -10.65), its last sample is 0. (2) The loop crossfade moves the cut up to 30 ms to the best-correlated offset and picks the law by the correlation (above 0.5 linear, otherwise equal power with a divisor for the correlation that is left). n_ingenuity: correlation 0.961, shift 19.27 ms, linear, 50 ms level inside the zone -0.64 dB against its surroundings (was -4.78 dB). The 1.5 dB statement as literally worded could NOT be proven for the other three loops, and the report says so below: their zone sits in a part where the recording itself moves by more than that; the part the crossfade adds is within 1.5 dB for all four (-0.46, +1.14, +1.35, -0.14 dB). (3) fadeOutMs states the applied fade; appendedTailMs is its own field. Rebuilt twice through the lock, second run byte-identical; 5 sound files changed bytes (listed). All unittest suites and fetch.py --check pass; ratings.json hash unchanged.

perFinding.finding: 1 k_door_close_1: fade-out cut the loudest part
perFinding.cause: process_download faded the last 30 ms of every one-shot whose last millisecond was not silent, without asking where the loudest part lies. In k_door_close_1 the envelope maximum (1 ms moving average of the channel maximum of |x|) is at sample 25258 of 25373, 2.4 ms before the end, so the fade multiplied it down (envelope maximum 3.09 dB lower) and the level step then turned the rest up (gain -10.65 dB against -14.09 dB for the unprocessed recording).
perFinding.change: New envelope_peak_index and _tail_out in build.py. In process_download: where the last ms is not silent, k = min(30 ms, n // 2) as before; if the envelope maximum lies at or after n - k (inside the fade that would be applied) the recording is left untouched and 144 samples (3 ms) of a raised cosine falling from the last sample to exactly zero are appended per channel (info.appendedTailMs 3.0, fadeOutMs 0.0); otherwise the fade stays. The test is against the fade that would really be applied, not a fixed 30 ms, so a file shorter than 60 ms (fade n // 2) is only changed when its maximum is inside that shorter fade.

numbers.k_door_close_1 after: appendedTailMs 3.0, fadeOutMs 0.0, duration 0.5316 s (3 ms longer), gain applied -14.09 dB, gain the unprocessed recording needs -14.09 dB (difference 0.00 dB, computed with set_level on the unprocessed prepare_download output), true peak -14.00 dBFS, last sample exactly 0, first sample -90.3 dBFS, no lead-in
numbers.check of all 29 one-shots: envelope maximum inside the last 30 ms: k_door_close_1 (2.4 ms from the end) and k_tick_2 (22.7 ms from the end of a 25 ms file); inside the fade that would really be applied: only k_door_close_1. k_tick_2's fade is 11.6 ms (n // 2) and its maximum lies before it, so it keeps its fade and does not change. Only k_door_close_1 changed among the one-shots.

perFinding.tests: class EndsLoudestAtTheEnd in tools/audio/tests/test_downloads_build.py: recording untouched and tail of 3 ms with the exact shape, last sample 0, length +144; gain equals the unprocessed need within 0.1 dB and peak at the target; tail per channel (stereo); maximum before the fade keeps the fade; short file with the maximum in its first half keeps its (10 ms) fade; silent end gets neither; envelope_peak_index. Existing test_only_the_loud_end_is_faded now uses a decaying sine (a steady sine has an arbitrary envelope maximum).

perFinding.finding: 2 n_ingenuity: dip in the crossfade zone
perFinding.cause: Tail and head of the steady 84 Hz tone are out of phase at the cut (the period is 11.9 ms, the file length is not a multiple of it); the equal-power law only keeps the level for unrelated signals, two phase-mismatched copies of one tone partly cancel.
perFinding.change: _loop_crossfade now (a) searches the cut up to 30 ms earlier (1440 candidates, fft cross-correlation, normalised, summed over channels, no mean removed, smallest shift on a tie) and takes the offset with the highest correlation over the crossfade length, (b) chooses the law by that correlation: above 0.5 linear (weights add to 1), otherwise cos / sin with the divisor 1 / sqrt(1 + c sin 2theta) (c clipped to 0 .. 0.5) that takes out the part of the correlation that plain equal power would add (c = 0 gives exactly cos / sin). The divisor is my addition to the stated rule: without it rover_driving (c 0.35) came out +2.65 dB in the zone. (c) The shift is applied to every loop, noise included, as the best-aligned offset; for noise it is a small gain over 0 and does no harm. info and checks get loopShiftMs, loopCorrelation, loopLaw and loopZone {vsOutsideDb, vsSourcesDb, outsideSpreadDb}; a loop whose vsSourcesDb exceeds 1.5 dB fails with the flag loop-crossfade-level (none does). The loop check and _loop_roll are unchanged.

numbers.metric: 50 ms windows every 10 ms inside the 300 ms zone, power mean over samples and channels, in dB against the mean power of the 300 ms before and the 300 ms after the zone ('literal': includes whatever the recording does there); 'outside range' is the same measure for all other windows of the loop. Computed by an independent scratch script on the processed files, and by build.py itself (checks.loopZone).

perFinding.not proven: The request asked that for every loop the 50 ms level inside the zone stays within 1.5 dB of the level just outside it. For n_ingenuity that holds (-0.64 dB). For cassini_saturn_1, plasma_hiss and rover_driving the literal figures above are +3.6, -20.6 and +6.9 dB, and they were about the same before my change; the same measure taken over the rest of the loop spans -4.2 .. +14.6, -23.9 .. +9.8 and -24.3 .. +7.9 dB, so these recordings move by more than 1.5 dB within a few hundred ms anywhere (plasma_hiss has a deep valley where its quiet end meets its quiet start: zone windows -52 .. -34 dB between -55 and -32 dB neighbours). Processing at the seam cannot remove that without cutting different material, which is a matter of the excerpts in selection.json (not mine). What the crossfade itself adds, measured against the power of the two mixed segments with the law's own weights, is within 1.5 dB for all four loops (-0.46, +1.14, +1.35, -0.14).
perFinding.also noticed: n_ingenuity has dips of 3.1 dB (at 4.35 s) and 3.9 dB (at 7.65 s) elsewhere in the file, far from the seam; they were there before and come from the recording (not examined further).
perFinding.tests: class TonalLoops: out-of-phase 84 Hz tone (n = 6 s + 137 samples, noise 0.01): the old cos / sin law is off by more than 1.5 dB in the zone, the new one is within 1.5 dB; shift between 0 and 30 ms equals the argmax of the correlation, law linear, correlation above 0.9; whole process: zone level, loop check, tiled joins; uncorrelated noise gets equal power and keeps its level; a noise with 0.36 shared power gets equal power with the correction and stays within 1.5 dB. Existing length assertions of Loops and Resampling now subtract the shift.

perFinding.cause: info['fadeOutMs'] was set to the constant FADE_OUT_MS although the code fades n // 2 samples in a short file (k_tick_2: 25 ms file, fade 11.6 ms).
perFinding.change: checks.fadeOutMs is now the applied fade in ms (k * 1000 / 48000, 3 decimals); the appended tail is checks.appendedTailMs (0.0 where none). Loops additionally carry loopShiftMs, loopCorrelation, loopLaw, loopZone. README (tools/audio/README.md) describes all of it.

notVerified: Nothing about how any sound sounds, including whether the zone of any loop is still audible as a pulse.
The literal 1.5 dB statement for cassini_saturn_1, plasma_hiss and rover_driving is not met and cannot be met at the seam (see not proven).

The envelope is the 1 ms moving average of the channel maximum; other definitions were not tried. The maximum of a steady tone is arbitrary (first maximum is taken), so such a file may get the tail instead of the fade by chance; none of the 29 one-shots is affected.
The correlation threshold 0.5 is as stated; at exactly 0.5 a linear fade of uncorrelated-in-part material dips about 1.25 dB in the middle.
The audition page and its capture check were not run (no server started); the click detector and the page faults of the previous report are not touched by this change.
The ratings tied to the hashes of the five changed files will show them as changed.
